farandwide.configuration.pauseModScreens: Pause Game While Mod Screens Are Open
When enabled, Far And Wide screens pause single-player like the normal pause menu. When disabled, routes, vehicles, and the world continue running.

screen.farandwide.help.title: Far And Wide Help
screen.farandwide.help.index.title: Help Index
screen.farandwide.help.index.body:
The primary purpose of the Far And Wide mod is to automate the movement of 'Vehicles' in Minecraft.

Originally the only supported Vehicle was the boat, but it grew to support mounts like horses and donkeys, and even the player themselves!

Secondarily, it also allows you to define cargo transfer points, so that Vehicles can automatically load and unload items at specific locations.
screen.farandwide.help.routes.title: Routes
screen.farandwide.help.routes.body: Vehicle automation is accomplished via the use of Routes.  You define a Route, assign it to a Vehicle, and activate it.
screen.farandwide.help.create.title: 1. Create a Route
screen.farandwide.help.create.body:
Open the Create Route screen using the Create Route command.

A Route requires a name and a traversal type.  The traversal type determines how the Vehicle will behave when it reaches the end of the route (end the route, loop, or reverse direction).
screen.farandwide.help.select.title: 2. Select a Route
screen.farandwide.help.select.body:
There may be multiple Routes available.  From the Route Management screen, select the Route you want to use.  The selected Route is always shown on the screen.

When you create a new Route, it will be selected automatically.
screen.farandwide.help.waypoints.title: 3. Add Waypoints
screen.farandwide.help.waypoints.body:
Manually travel the intended Route, adding Waypoints as you go.

To add the player's current position as a Waypoint, use the Add Or Remove Waypoint command.  Using a Minecraft hotkey for this command makes it much easier.
screen.farandwide.help.assign.title: 4. Assign a Route
screen.farandwide.help.assign.body:
Once the Route has been defined, assign it to a supported Vehicle.  To do that, mount the Vehicle and use the Assign Route command.

If you assign a Route without being in a Vehicle, the Route will be assigned directly to the player, in which case you can traverse the Route yourself!
screen.farandwide.help.activate.title: 5. Activate a Route
screen.farandwide.help.activate.body:
Once a Route is assigned to one or more Vehicles, activate it using the Toggle Route command.

All Vehicles assigned to that Route will automatically travel to each Waypoint in the Route, following the traversal type defined for it.
screen.farandwide.help.cargo.title: Cargo
screen.farandwide.help.cargo.body:
Automated movement is cool, but cargo transport takes the mod to the next level!

This feature allows you to automate item transfer over vast distances without the exorbitant expenditure of time and resources to build huge networks of railways, pipes, or conveyors.
screen.farandwide.help.cargo.create.body:
Edit a Waypoint by 'using' it (default: right-click).

Switch it to a Cargo Waypoint, and then select whether you want to load cargo, unload cargo, or both at that Waypoint.
screen.farandwide.help.cargo.stations.bo:
A 'Station' is an inventory (like a chest) linked to a Cargo Waypoint.

To create a Load or Unload Station, click the appropriate button on the Edit Waypoint screen, and then 'use' (default: right-click) the inventory you want to link.
When a Vehicle with an inventory (e.g., a boat or donkey with an assigned chest) arrives at a Cargo Waypoint, it will load and/or unload items to/from the linked Stations.

After completing all transfers, the Vehicle will continue to the next Waypoint.
screen.farandwide.help.tips_and_tricks.p:
- The Add Or Remove Waypoint command is context-sensitive.  If you are looking at a Waypoint, it will be removed.  Otherwise, your current position will be added as a new Waypoint.

- New Waypoints are added just in front of the player's current position, rather than exactly on it, so you can more easily see it being added.

- Waypoints have adjustable radii, so you can make them larger or smaller depending on how precise you want the Vehicle to be when it arrives at a Waypoint.

- Waypoint order can be adjusted in the Waypoint Editor, so you can add a new Waypoint in the middle of a Route and adjust it to the correct position without having to delete anything.

- The Toggle Route command starts or stops every Vehicle on the selected Route.  The Toggle Vehicle command starts or stops *only* the currently mounted Vehicle.

- If you expand a Route on the Route Management screen, you will see every Vehicle assigned to that Route.

- Vehicles will be listed in the Route Management screen with generic names (e.g., 'horse 1') unless tagged with a name tag.

- As usual you can name horses, donkeys, and mules with name tags, but in Far And Wide you can also use name tags on boats!  This allows you to give a recognizable name to every supported Vehicle.

- Automated movement does not use ANY pathfinding.  It simply moves the Vehicle in a straight line to the next Waypoint.  So make sure your Routes are clear of obstacles!

- Yes, the player's movement can be automated!  If you use the Assign Route command without being mounted on a Vehicle, it will be assigned to the player.  Then just activate the Route and let it take you there!

- Automated horses, donkeys and mules move twice as fast when mounted by the player.  This is intentional.

- A Vehicle on a One Way traversal stops at the Route's last Waypoint, but if you start that Vehicle again using the Toggle Vehicle command or the 'Start Vehicle' button on the Route Management screen, it will do another One Way traversal in the opposite direction.

- You may specify item filters on the Edit Waypoint screen to specify which items may be picked up or dropped off at that Cargo Waypoint.

- Cargo Stations are not limited to chests.  Any inventory block (like a furnace, barrel, or hopper) can be used as a Cargo Station.

- When you select a Cargo Station, you actually specify one of the block's faces.  This allows you to do things like putting raw food in the top face of a furnace and taking the cooked items out of the bottom, or putting items in the top face of a hopper and taking them out of its 'nozzle' side.

- Keep in mind the distinction between a 'selected' Route (the one you're currently working with) and an 'assigned' Route (one that a Vehicle is using).  You can't assign a Route until you have first selected it.

- Currently the mod supports boats, horses, donkeys, mules, and the player themselves as Vehicles, and only 'chest boats' and 'chest donkeys/mules' are supported as Cargo transports.  But more types may be added in the future.

- The mod is designed to work in both single-player and multiplayer mode, but it has not been tested in multiplayer yet.

- The mod loads chunks around Vehicles that are on active Routes, so that they can continue to move even if the player is far away.

traversal.farandwide.one_way.description: Stop at each end, return to that endpoint when restarted, then travel in the opposite direction.
traversal.farandwide.loop.description: Return to the first waypoint after reaching the last.  Only useful for routes with more than one waypoint.
traversal.farandwide.reverse.description: Reverse direction at each end of the route.  Only useful for routes with more than one waypoint.
